papers.title: Surface modification of dental implants - A narrative review
papers.abstract: The dental implants have proven to be the most desired method of a replacement of the missing teeth, with the success rates of the dental implants reported to be between 90-99 per cent in the existing literature. Osseointegration, which is the close structural and functional bonding of viable bone tissue and the implant surface, is the key to the sustained performance of an implant. Surface modification has become the primary approach to improving the process of osseointegration, reducing the risk of peri-implant infections, and extending the total lifespan of implants. This narrative review will cover the history, classification, mechanism, and clinical outcomes of the surface modification methods of dental implants. Those methods covered in the review are subtractive techniques, like machining, sandblasting, and acid-etching, additive techniques, like hydroxyapatite (HA) coating and titanium plasma spraying (TPS), chemical techniques, including anodization, alkali treatment, and fluoride incorporation, and biochemical functionalization with growth factors, peptides, and drug-eluting systems. State-of-the-art technologies, such as nanoengineering, laser surface texturing, zirconia and PEEK modifications along with antimicrobial approaches are also discussed. Existing literature invariably advocates moderately rough surfaces (Ra = 102μm) as the most preferable in bone-implant contact, and the multifunctional coating of osteogenic and antibacterial properties as the future of the science of implant surfaces.

papers.title: A Neuro-Physical Framework for Three-Dimensional Elastodynamic Wave Prediction in Mechanical Components
papers.abstract: Predicting vibration-wave propagation in mechanical components requires solvingtransient, three-dimensional elastodynamic equations across complex geometries, material interfaces, and frequency-dependent damping. This paper proposes a researchframework—termed the Causal Energy-Constrained Neural Operator (CENOp)—for learning mappings from material properties, geometry, initial conditions, andexternal excitation to displacement, velocity, and stress fields.The framework combines continuum mechanics with a neural operator, enforcingmomentum balance, constitutive consistency, boundary and interface conditions, andan energy-dissipation inequality. A memory-variable constitutive model representslinear viscoelastic damping, while optional stochastic fields represent materialuncertainty. The proposed additions are hypotheses for future testing, not establishedphysical laws.A reproducible validation program is outlined using analytical wave solutions,finite-element simulations, and measurements from instrumented components. Theframework is intended as a fast surrogate for repeated forward predictions andas a tool for parameter identification, damage localization, and uncertainty-awarestructural monitoring. Its performance must be demonstrated against independentnumerical and experimental benchmarks before engineering use.

papers.title: Bayesian Hybrid Surrogate Modeling of Algorithmic Tangent Stiffness Matrices in Elastoplastic Materials
papers.abstract: The algorithmic tangent stiffness is the local derivative of the discrete constitutive stress update with respect to the strain increment. It is therefore central tothe convergence, stability, and computational cost of implicit finite-element analyses of plastic materials. This paper develops a physics-informed Bayesian hybridsurrogate framework for predicting stress and algorithmic tangent responses fromexpensive constitutive integrations. The reference constitutive structure is smallstrain associative von Mises plasticity with isotropic hardening, integrated by animplicit return-mapping algorithm. Its consistent tangent is derived by linearizingthe discrete update, rather than by differentiating a continuous-time rate equation in isolation. A Gaussian-process surrogate is then defined for the constitutive correction,with its tangent obtained as the derivative of the posterior mean. The proposedhybrid construction combines an analytical elastic or mechanistic baseline with aprobabilistic correction and imposes symmetry and thermodynamic admissibilitythrough parameterization, constraints, or explicit diagnostics. Bayesian calibration,heteroscedastic observation noise, active learning, and finite-element equilibriumcoupling are formulated in a unified notation. The work is a mathematical andcomputational framework; it does not claim a new experimental data set or reportnumerical validation results. A verification protocol is specified to assess stress error,tangent error, posterior calibration, dissipation, and global Newton convergencebefore engineering deployment.

papers.title: Plasma‐Enabled Multiscale Coupling of Gyroid Architecture and Silver Nanoparticle Biointerfaces Drives Osteogenesis in 3D‐Printed Scaffolds
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering functional bone scaffolds can be enhanced by integrating biologically instructive nanoscale surface features (e.g., nanotopography and nanoroughness), micro‐scale geometric cues (e.g., curvature and porosity), and macro‐scale mechanical properties (e.g., bulk stiffness); however, these length scales are often optimized independently. Here, we present a multiscale design framework combining additive manufacturing of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gyroid scaffolds with plasma‐assisted nanoscale surface engineering to regulate osteogenesis. Controlled variation in strut thickness generates distinct architectural regimes with coupled changes in curvature, porosity, and compressive modulus, recapitulating key aspects of trabecular bone mechanics. Micro‐computed tomography confirms trabecular bone‐like features, while finite element modeling and compression testing reveal that thinner architectures (0.6 mm) exhibit curvature‐preserving geometry and distributed stress profiles favorable for cellular interaction. A low‐temperature plasma electroless reduction (PER) strategy enables controlled silver nanoparticle (AgNP) deposition, while polydopamine (PDA) ensures uniform, cytocompatible coatings. Notably, PDA‐AgNP‐functionalized 0.6 mm scaffolds exhibit enhanced cytoskeletal organization, mineralization, and osteogenic gene expression, accompanied by elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) and YAP/TAZ ‐associated transcriptional activity. These findings support cross‐scale coupling of architecture and nanoscale biointerfaces as a design framework for osteogenic scaffolds.

papers.title: Bayesian Synchronization of Proxy Paleorecords with Reference Chronologies
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Many scientific fields compare two or more noisy time series that integrate the same process but are recorded on different time scales. In paleoclimate studies, for example, proxy measurements are collected versus stratigraphic depth in a climate archive and then converted to calendar time. Synchronizing two proxy records often requires estimating an alignment that maps the depth (or preliminary age) of an input record onto the calendar‐time scale of an absolutely‐dated target record so that corresponding proxy signals line up. Existing alignment approaches are generally optimization‐based and return a single transformation, providing limited formal uncertainty quantification. Here, we introduce BSync, a Bayesian synchronization framework that treats alignments as inference over a monotone time‐mapping function to match an input to a target record. The alignment is expressed as a transformation of the input depth (or age) scale to match the target record, achieved through a link function that locally expands and compresses the input scale. The model is parameterized through interpretable local rate parameters, enabling the specification of priors on deposition times to regularize the alignment toward physically plausible deformations. BSync jointly infers the aligned chronology and provides posterior uncertainty for the time‐warping function and the resulting age scale. In synthetic data experiments and a real‐data case study, BSync yields well‐calibrated credible intervals for the aligned time scale and achieves more accurate alignments than a state‐of‐the‐art automated method, particularly when independent age constraints are sparse.

papers.title: Enhancing student engagement in higher education: Collaborative online international learning across Nordic universities
papers.abstract: This paper examines how Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL), supported by active learning methods, enhances student engagement in higher education. The paper builds on a collaboration among three universities in the Nordic countries (Finland, Norway, and Sweden) and a joint course module focused on sustainability conducted over two years, involving a total of 510 students. The primary learning outcomes for the three courses are in the topic area of industrial marketing and purchasing, specifically analyzing firms' business networks to manage interorganizational relationships, including the firms' marketing, purchasing, and supply chain processes. The module, designed as hybrid COIL, is project-based, including synchronous and asynchronous tasks completed in small groups by applying various active learning methods. Student engagement is analyzed across five dimensions: Social, Cognitive, Behavioral, Collaborative, and Emotional. The paper develops a framework that illustrates how COIL and active learning methods enhance student engagement. The combination of tasks with group-based active learning methods is highly important, impacting students’ perceptions of engagement. Peer meetings across universities in small student groups stand out as vastly important in engaging students.

papers.title: Adaptive active learning and metaheuristic-optimized transformer framework for robust intrusion detection in software-defined networks
papers.abstract: Abstract Existing intrusion detection systems largely rely on static supervised learning models that require extensive labeled data and periodic retraining. Such approaches struggle to adapt to evolving attack patterns in dynamic software-defined networks. To address these limitations, this study proposes an adaptive intrusion detection framework that integrates uncertainty-driven active learning, metaheuristic-based feature selection, Transformer-based attack classification, and adaptive hyperparameter optimization within a unified software-defined networking architecture. Unlike conventional adaptive intrusion detection systems that rely on static feature representations or fixed learning strategies, the proposed framework continuously refines both the training data and model configuration to improve robustness against evolving cyberattacks. The proposed framework iteratively identifies informative samples for annotation, optimizes feature subsets using adaptive search, and continuously updates the classifier to maintain high detection performance under changing traffic distributions. The proposed system was evaluated using the ToN-IoT dataset and additional real-world traffic traces. Experimental evaluation on benchmark and real-world network traffic datasets demonstrated a detection accuracy of up to 97.92% and an F1-score of 97.10%. Although the optimization stage increases offline training time, the optimized model maintains efficient inference during deployment, making it suitable for practical software-defined network environments. Performance was evaluated over five independent runs using different random initialization seeds. Although the optimization and active-learning stages increase offline training time, the optimized model maintains efficient inference during deployment. Performance was evaluated over five independent runs using different random initialization seeds. The results demonstrate that the complementary use of adaptive sample acquisition, feature selection, and hyperparameter optimization provides an effective intrusion-detection framework for software-defined network environments.

papers.title: Assessing the Perceived Effectiveness and Identifying Challenges of In-Service Training for Staff in a Teaching Hospital: A Mixed-Method, Sequential Explanatory Study
papers.abstract: Background: In-service training of healthcare staff is one of the key components of professional development and improving the quality of services. However, previous evidence indicates that the extent of applying learned material in the workplace can be influenced by individual, organizational, and process factors. This study aimed to evaluate the perceived effectiveness of in-service training and identify its challenges and harms from the perspectives of staff and managers in a teaching hospital in Yazd. Methods: This study was conducted using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design in 2024–2025. In the quantitative phase, 309 employees were selected through stratified random sampling proportional to size and completed Esmaili’s 24-item In-Service Training Effectiveness Questionnaire. This instrument assesses employees’ perceptions of the effect of training on three dimensions: knowledge development, skill improvement, and attitude creation/change, using a 5-point Likert scale, with a total score range of 24–120. Quantitative data were analyzed using independent t-tests and one-way analysis of variance with SPSS 26. In the qualitative phase, quantitative findings were used to gain a deeper understanding of employees’ perceptions of training effectiveness and to guide the interviews. At this stage, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 purposively selected managers and employees. Qualitative data were analyzed using directed thematic analysis based on the structural, process, and contextual dimensions of the three-pronged model using MaxQDA 2020 software. Results: The mean total perceived effectiveness score was 87.57 ± 27.68 (out of 120; 73% of the maximum). The mean scores for knowledge development, skill improvement, and attitude creation/change were 21.86 ± 6.71 (out of 30), 25.79 ± 7.88 (out of 35), and 39.91 ± 13.43 (out of 55), respectively; after standardization for the number of items, the three dimensions were at a similar level (72.6 % to 73.7 % of the maximum). Scores on all three dimensions differed significantly by job group, educational level, employment status, and work experience (P < 0.001). By gender, skill improvement (P = 0.045) and attitude change (P = 0.019) differed significantly, and by age, only skill improvement did (P = 0.017). Qualitative analysis revealed the challenges of the staff training system in three main themes: structural challenges (time constraints and work pressure, poor needs assessment and educational planning, limited resources and educational infrastructure, and inadequate managerial support and motivational system); process challenges (mismatch of course content with job needs, challenges related to instructors, dominance of passive teaching methods, and poor evaluation and feedback); and contextual challenges (insufficient continuous learning culture, inadequate motivation for participation, participants' perception of limited training transfer, and reduced perceived value of training). Conclusion: The findings of this study indicate that although employees and managers have a positive attitude and relative acceptance toward in-service training, this process faces serious challenges in needs assessment, design, implementation, evaluation, and post-training support. These limitations play a key role, particularly in the application of learning in the workplace. To improve perceived effectiveness and facilitate the transfer of learning to the operational environment, revising training policies is essential. This revision should focus on accurate needs assessment based on job descriptions, designing practical content with active learning methods, empowering instructors, and especially strengthening managerial support and continuous evaluation systems.

papers.title: Addressing AIAA Aerodynamics Uncertainty Quantification Challenge with Sensitivity-Based and Diffusion Model Updating
papers.abstract: This paper presents the principles and techniques employed to address the AIAA Second Uncertainty Quantification Challenge Problem for Aerodynamics. Two distinct model updating strategies for uncertainty quantification and reduction are investigated: a sensitivity-based approach and a data-driven diffusion-model-based approach. Both methods aim to infer the posterior distributions of key aerodynamic input parameters, which are subsequently propagated through either a surrogate model or XFOIL to obtain posterior-predictive lift, drag, and moment coefficients. The diffusion model shows consistent posterior-predictive responses across both the surrogate and XFOIL, whereas the sensitivity-based approach produces sharply concentrated parameter posteriors that may represent a more limited uncertainty range. Across multiple operating configurations, the two approaches produce coherent predictive aerodynamic responses despite their differing parameter posterior structures. The findings suggest that, in uncertainty quantification challenges of this type, it is not only essential to characterize multiple sources of uncertainty but equally, if not more, critical to employ an appropriate inverse uncertainty-reduction mechanism capable of leveraging the necessarily limited observational data. Designing such inverse processes to extract maximal information from sparse data remains a central difficulty and an important direction for future research in aerodynamic uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: A Cloud Learning‐Analytics Framework for Multi‐Tier Engineering Education: A Mixed‐Methods Implementation Case Study Across Three Avionics Courses
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Computer‐application‐mediated learning analytics can connect simulation, controlled measurement, and field practice, but engineering‐course evidence is fragmented across instruments and units of analysis. This article contributes (1) an adaptation‐oriented four‐stage spiral curriculum with a six‐step weekly micro‐routine and (2) an implementation‐oriented cloud learning‐analytics framework for organising evidence. The curriculum ran for one academic year across three courses as a bounded single‐site case; the framework was specified but not analytically validated. Only Radar Systems and Microwave Engineering had traceable outcome summaries. An enrolment audit identified 49 records for 45 unique students; after one withdrawal, 48 completion records represented 44 students. The quantitatively driven convergent design combined course‐level summaries with 42 archived Radar Systems text entries (43 coded segments) as embedded qualitative evidence. The institutional report documented a Radar Systems knowledge improvement of at least 20% on the pre/post test and a pass‐rate change from 63% to 81%; Microwave Engineering recorded a project mean of 82.5/100 (4/4 groups ≥ 80). Feedback concerned gamified engagement, peer learning, reduced boredom, memory reinforcement, and active learning. Kahoot! records re‐exported during revision show a same‐cohort improvement of +16.9 percentage points (Hedges g av = 1.08) for the 22 students attending both first and final quiz sessions—not an equivalent‐form pre/post gain, because sessions covered different units; an alternative pairing of 31 students yields −4.8 points (non‐significant). Otherwise, item‐level responses, paired knowledge‐test records, and rater‐level scores were not retained, so reliability coefficients, effect sizes, and confidence intervals are not reported. The results support implementation feasibility and plausible learning mechanisms, not causal efficacy.

papers.title: Multi-objective artificial pedosphere intelligence for microbial homeostasis-oriented governance of functional nanoparticle systems in complex ecosystems
papers.abstract: Abstract Soil microbial homeostasis is fundamental to sustainable agriculture and ecological resilience, yet existing machine learning approaches primarily emphasize prediction accuracy while overlooking microbial interactions, uncertainty quantification, ecological homeostasis, and decision-support for nanoparticle governance. This study proposes an Artificial Pedosphere Intelligence framework to predict the Microbial Homeostasis Deviation Score (MHDS) by integrating a Microbial Co-occurrence Graph Attention Network (MC-GAT), homeostasis-constrained learning, a Deep Kernel Gaussian Process (DKL), Bayesian Multi-Objective Optimization, and SHAP-based explainability within a unified ecological intelligence pipeline. The framework first constructs an ecological feature graph, learns biologically informed representations, estimates predictive uncertainty, and subsequently performs simulation-based optimization to identify environmentally balanced nanoparticle governance strategies. The model was implemented using Python 3.10 with PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric, GPyTorch, BoTorch, and SHAP, and evaluated on the Kaggle Soil Microbe Dataset containing 100,000 soil samples. The proposed framework achieved R² = 0.962, MSE = 0.007, and MAE = 0.016, representing an approximately 2.3% improvement in R² over the strongest baseline (0.94). These findings demonstrate that biologically informed graph intelligence combined with uncertainty-aware optimization provides accurate, interpretable, and scalable ecological decision support for sustainable soil management. .

papers.title: Co-Intelligence in Practice: Qualitative Research Education With AI
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) is increasingly integrated into higher education, raising methodological and ethical questions for qualitative research instruction. This article examines how we, three experienced qualitative research instructors, integrated GAI tools into our graduate-level research methods courses. Our pedagogical approach to integrating GAI tools is situated within the broader literature on GAI in higher education and qualitative research instruction, emphasizing active learning and technological reflexivity. Our work is also guided by Ethan Mollick’s artificial intelligence (AI) principles from Co-Intelligence: Living and Working with AI. Using reflective narrative case examples, we demonstrate how Mollick’s principles guided ethical and methodologically responsive integration of GAI, challenged assumptions about rigor and trustworthiness, and reconfigured instructor–student relationships. We conclude by highlighting tensions between efficiency, inclusion, and epistemic responsibility and implications for qualitative research education.

papers.title: Effect of Annealing Heat Treatment on Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Ti-6242 Alloy Fabricated by Laser Powder Bed Fusion Method
papers.abstract: Introduction and Objectives: Ti-6242 alloy is highly regarded in additive manufacturing due to its excellent thermal resistance. Titanium laser-based additively manufactured components, however, often require post-heat treatments because of their high solidification rate and formation of undesirable phases. The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of annealing heat treatment on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Ti-6242 specimens fabricated by laser powder bed fusion method. Materials and Methods: Annealing heat treatments were conducted at three temperatures of 950, 1005, and 1050 ℃ for holding times of 1, 3, 5, and 7 hours. The resulting microstructure, phase composition, and mechanical properties were characterized using optical and scanning electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and shear punch testing. Results: The as-built microstructure consisted of columnar primary β grains with colonies of metastable martensitic α′. Heat treatment led to decomposition of α′ and formation of more stable α and β phases. At 1005 and 1050 °C, the microstructure transformed from columnar to equiaxed, whereas at 950 °C, the columnar structure was retained. Williamson–Hall plots obtained from XRD patterns revealed a reduction in the lattice microstrain of heat treated samples compared with the as-built one. The applied heat treatment, improved both ultimate shear strength and ductility of the samples. The highest ultimate shear strength (761 MPa) and normalized displacement (0.638) were achieved at 1005 °C. Conclusion: Appropriate heat treatment leads to a more stable microstructure, reduction in lattice microstrain, and transformation of the columnar structure to an equiaxed one. This process could simultaneously enhance the ultimate shear strength and ductility compared to the as-built sample.

papers.title: Thermo‐Hydraulic Performance Enhancement of Microchannel Heat Sinks: A Review of Passive Techniques and Emerging AI/ML Approaches
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The rapid advancement of modern electronics resulted in intensified thermal management challenges, and positioned microchannel heat sinks (MCHSs) as a promising technology to dissipate high heat fluxes in next generation electronics. This review critically examines recent developments in passive thermo‐hydraulic enhancement of MCHSs, with emphasis on three major approaches: channel geometry modification, internal flow modifying structures, and working fluid enhancement. The reviewed studies are synthesized according to their underlying heat transfer mechanisms, including secondary flow generation, boundary layer redevelopment, vortex‐induced mixing, wake interaction, recirculation, and increased effective heat transfer area. Particular emphasis is placed on the balance between heat transfer enhancement and hydraulic losses, as an increase in Nusselt number alone does not necessarily indicate better thermo‐hydraulic performance. The review considers integrated and hybrid enhancement configurations, as the combined use of different flow disturbing elements provided improved heat transfer with properly designed interaction. Excessive flow blockage resulted in a pressure drop penalty and reduces the overall benefit. Nanofluids and hybrid nanofluids are also discussed, considering their potential to enhance thermal performance as well as practical concerns such as stability, increased viscosity, particle sedimentation, and higher pumping requirements. In addition, emerging AI/ML approaches are reviewed across performance prediction, deep learning, physics‐informed modelling, surrogate‐assisted optimization, reinforcement learning, and CFD–ML frameworks. The analysis indicates that AI/ML can accelerate design exploration and optimization within defined parameter domains, but limitations associated with dataset quality, extrapolation, uncertainty, and independent validation remain. Finally, key research gaps involving experimental validation, manufacturability, multi‐parameter optimization, transient thermal behavior, uncertainty quantification, and intelligent thermal control are identified. The review provides an integrated perspective for developing high performance and practically viable MCHSs for next‐generation electronics cooling.

papers.title: A High‐Throughput Diffusion Couple Strategy for Optimizing the Composition of Fe–14Cr–2Y 2 O 3 ‐Based Oxide Dispersion‐Strengthened Steel With Densely Distributed Oxide Nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Oxide dispersion‐strengthened (ODS) alloys have been widely studied due to their excellent high‐temperature creep performance and good resistance to radiation damage. However, the conventional mechanical alloying process is associated with a prolonged preparation cycle, challenges in composition control, and limited reproducibility, posing significant obstacles to the compositional design of ODS alloys. Here, we propose a new strategy for effectively screening the composition, microstructure, and properties of Fe–14Cr–2Y 2 O 3 ‐based ODS alloys via a diffusion couple technique. A continuous Ti–Al composition gradient is established within a single diffusion couple, enabling simultaneous evaluation of multiple compositions under identical processing conditions. The inter‐diffusivity along the diffusion path is determined for alloying elements with corresponding uncertainty quantification. A Ti/(Ti + Al) ratio of 0.7 is identified as optimal, yielding a high nanoparticle number density of 7.5 × 10 22 m −3 and an average particle size of ~6 nm—performance metrics that significantly outperform those achieved at other ratios. Correspondingly, the Vickers hardness reaches a peak value of 315.8 HV at Ti/(Ti + Al) ≈0.77, attributed to the synergistic effects of dispersion strengthening and solid solution strengthening. This study establishes a rational, composition‐driven strategy for the high‐throughput design of ODS alloys tailored for nuclear applications, demonstrating that the diffusion couple technique can achieve rapid correlation and efficient screening of composition–microstructure–property relationships.
